display.purpose: The name in the stacked (mobile) rail. One name is visible at a time.

headline.purpose: Section headings, preceded by a short sage rule.

title.purpose: Role line, card heads, timeline roles.

body.purpose: Running text, max 62-65ch (set per paragraph, not on the column).

body-small.purpose: Tagline, timeline, bullets, credentials, recommendations, footer.

hero-name.purpose: The name in the hero on the split layout; the one display-size moment (6rem ceiling).

terminal.purpose: The typed role line only: system monospace, imitates terminal input.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Hovered cards with translateY(-2px); allowed at rest only for the most important piece of a section.

motion.name: gsap-reveals
motion.value: GSAP + ScrollTrigger, gated by gsap.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)')
motion.purpose: Play once, never reverse: rail accent line draws in and stays (no idle loop, WCAG 2.2.2); section reveals; "Cómo trabajo" slope line draw-in.

motion.name: typed-role
motion.value: JS timers (no library): type 45ms/key, hold 600ms, erase 22ms/key, 160ms gap; plays once (~4.6s)
motion.purpose: The one authored motion moment: the hero role line types and erases two texts then rests on the real role. Caret blinks 3 times then goes. Reduced motion shows the final role immediately.

breakpoints.name: stacked
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: rail becomes a static header, single column.

breakpoints.name: short
breakpoints.purpose: Sticky rail steps its spacing down one notch so it fits ~768–800px-tall laptops.

breakpoints.name: touch
breakpoints.purpose: 44px targets; hover lifts off, :active feedback on.

breakpoints.name: ledger-container
breakpoints.purpose: Ledger rows stack the fact under the product name.

breakpoints.name: timeline-container
breakpoints.purpose: Timeline rows stack the label above the bar.

breakpoints.name: fluid-grids
breakpoints.value: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, X), 1fr)) with X = 26rem work, 22rem earlier work, 20rem recommendations, 16rem tech
breakpoints.purpose: No fixed column counts; the content column is fluid (max-width 88rem).

background.purpose: Flat paper over the whole viewport; the production dot pattern kept as a soft texture (6% alpha cap = contrast budget for Ink Faint). The production grey gradient was dropped 2026-10-05.

narrative.overview:
The site reads like a well-kept technical dossier: a fixed rail on the left (preferences, quick facts, CV and contact, jump-nav) and, on the right, a hero that gives the name at full scale and the proof of what runs today, followed by filed evidence (numbered work, a charted timeline, credentials, recommendations). Every visual device earns its place by organising or proving something: numbers index the work, boxed data points hold facts, one sparkline draws a real measured improvement (88% → 93%), and one bar chart places the career on a real time axis. Decoration that proves nothing does not belong.

Density is editorial and calm: a fluid content column that takes the space the rail leaves (capped only on ultra-wide screens) with reading measure set per paragraph (≤65ch), generous section spacing, small uppercase labels, a single desaturated accent used for marks rather than fills. Warmth comes from the serif headings and the off-white paper over the kept dotted-pattern background. Components are firm and tactile: they answer the pointer clearly (lift, shadow, accent border) instead of barely reacting.

Confirmed anti-references: the neon/gamer portfolio (the current production site: neon gradients, violets, Poppins, attention-grabbing effects) and the corporate CV (formal, grey, HR-document feel).
keyCharacteristics: Split layout: sticky fluid rail (`clamp(18rem, 20vw, 21rem)`) + a fluid content column that opens with the hero.
One accent (Sage Field), used as marks, rules, active states and status, never as large fills.
Serif display for names and section heads; system sans for everything else; one typed terminal line in system monospace.
Evidence drawn on real axes: the 88% → 93% slope and the 2013–today timeline share one grammar (open point = start, filled point = end).
Numbered, boxed, dated evidence: `01`, `02`… on work cards, bordered data points, date pills.
Light and dark themes with the same structure; flat paper everywhere with the production dot pattern as a soft texture.

rules.name: The AA Floor Rule
rules.body: Every text token clears 4.5:1 on Paper, Paper Raised _and_ Sage Field Wash, in both themes (measured minimum 4.62:1). Ink Faint and Sage Field Deep were darkened/lightened for this; new tokens must meet the same floor before use.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Sage Field is the only hue. No second accent, no gradients between hues; everything else is paper, ink and rule.

rules.name: The Mark, Not Fill Rule
rules.body: The accent appears as lines, dots, text, markers and 8–10% washes, never as a solid block behind content.

rules.name: The Serif Is a Signature Rule
rules.body: Georgia is reserved for the name, section headings, and numerals (work counters, quote mark, timeline years). Body, UI and data are always sans.

rules.name: The Typed Input Exception
rules.body: One line leaves the sans: the hero's typed role line uses the system monospace stack (`ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace`, no download) because it imitates terminal input. Nothing else on the page is monospace.

rules.name: The Quiet Label Rule
rules.body: Structure is labelled with small uppercase Ink Faint text, never with bigger or bolder headings.

rules.name: The Earned Lift Rule
rules.body: Elevation signals either interaction or importance. A piece may rest lifted only if it is the most important thing in its section.

dos: Do give the page one authored motion moment (the typed role line) and let everything else stay still or respond to the pointer; gate it behind `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do keep claims readable without interaction and put detail behind `<details>`, not behind hover.
Do keep a single accent (Sage Field family) and use it as marks: rules, dots, borders, text, 8–10% washes.
Do reserve Georgia for the name, section headings and numerals; everything else in the system sans.
Do give interactive elements a clear, tactile response: lift (`translateY(-2px)` + Lifted shadow) and/or accent border/underline, 200ms standard ease.
Do number and box evidence (work counters, data points, date pills) so the page reads as a filed dossier.
Do keep the page one continuous paper surface with the dot texture at ≤6% alpha, and support both themes with the same tokens.
Do gate GSAP motion behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` and zero out CSS transitions under reduced motion; keep `:focus-visible` outlines (2px Sage Field Deep, 2px offset).
donts: Don't loop or auto-scroll content (marquees, idle drifts, endless rotators): it fails WCAG 2.2.2 and the dossier tone. A motion sequence plays once and settles on the true state.
Don't draw a time axis that stops before the present or hides recent years: it makes live work read as stale. The timeline labels every year to 2026 and marks "Hoy".
Don't set a width in pixels as the layout: use `clamp`, `minmax`, `auto-fit` and container queries; pixels are limits.
Don't make a second monospace moment: the typed role line is the one exception to "sans for everything else".
Don't reintroduce the grey side-vignette gradient or any surface edge in the page background; a visible seam where the content ends was the reason it was dropped.
Don't drift toward the neon/gamer look of the current production site: no neon gradients, violets, Poppins/Oswald, glow shadows, or flashy effects.
Don't drift toward a corporate CV: no grey formality, no dense document tables, no stiff HR tone.
Don't add a second accent colour or fill large areas with the accent.
Don't add decoration that proves nothing; every illustrative element must organise or evidence real content (like the 88% → 93% slope chart, which plots only the two real measurements).
Don't put a thick coloured border on one side of a card or row; emphasis comes from elevation, structure and the accent as a mark.
Don't make hovers so faint they read as broken; components here are firm, not whisper-quiet.
